ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the left figure, object a is above and object b is below; the two are connected by a vertical light spring, and the external force F acts vertically upward on a; in the right figure, object b, the spring, and object a are placed in sequence on a smooth horizontal tabletop, and the external force F acts horizontally to the right on a. Then reason: Suppose the masses of the two objects are respectively m1 and m2. When pulling vertically upward, take a and b as a whole as the object of study, there is F-(m1+m2)g=(m1+m2)a1, so a1=F/(m1+m2)-g. Then analyze object b: in the vertical direction the spring tension T1 is upward, and the weight m2g is downward, therefore T1-m2g=m2a1; substituting a1 gives T1=m2F/(m1+m2). When pulling horizontally, take a and b as a whole as the object of study; on the smooth horizontal plane, in the horizontal direction there is only the external force F, so F=(m1+m2)a2, giving a2=F/(m1+m2). Then analyze object b: in the horizontal direction the spring tension T2 provides its acceleration, therefore T2=m2a2=m2F/(m1+m2). Thus T1=T2. A light spring satisfies Hooke's law T=kx, and the spring is the same, so x1=x2.

method.method_draft: 先读图：左图中物体a在上、b在下，中间竖直接轻弹簧，外力F竖直向上作用在a上；右图中b、弹簧、a依次放在光滑水平桌面上，外力F水平向右作用在a上。再读题：两物体质量分别为m1、m2，弹簧伸长量分别为x1、x2，且两次外力大小相同。用整体法先求两次共同加速度：竖直情形对a+b整体有F-(m1+m2)g=(m1+m2)a1，所以a1=F/(m1+m2)-g；水平情形有F=(m1+m2)a2，所以a2=F/(m1+m2)。再分别对物体b列牛顿第二定律：竖直时弹簧拉力T1满足T1-m2g=m2a1，代入得T1=m2F/(m1+m2)；水平时弹簧拉力T2满足T2=m2a2，得T2=m2F/(m1+m2)。因此T1=T2。由轻弹簧胡克定律T=kx，得x1=x2。

method.method_draft: 先读图：左图表示a、弹簧、b沿竖直方向排布，F向上拉a；右图表示b、弹簧、a沿水平光滑桌面排布，F向右拉a。再读题：两次外力大小都是F，弹簧轻质，系统做共同匀加速运动。用“相对运动/有效外力分配”观点：由于a、b保持相对静止地共同加速，弹簧伸长只由需要传递给b的那部分非公共外力决定。竖直情形中，重力同时作用于a和b，且按质量成比例，是公共体力；它只改变整体加速度中的-g部分，不造成a、b间额外相对拉伸。真正由a通过弹簧传给b的，是外加拉力F按质量比例分给b的份额，即T1=m2/(m1+m2)·F。水平光滑情形中，重力和支持力在竖直方向平衡，水平方向只有外力F使系统加速；b同样需要得到整个外力F中按质量比例属于它的份额，即T2=m2/(m1+m2)·F。因此T1=T2，轻弹簧劲度系数相同，所以x1=x2。

Try to compare the magnitude relationship between $x_1$ and $x_2$.
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The masses of objects a and b are respectively $m_1$ and $m_2$, and they are connected by a light spring. When a constant force $F$ is used to pull a vertically upward, making a and b together do uniformly accelerated linear motion upward, the elongation of the spring is $x_1$; when a constant force whose magnitude is still $F$ is used to pull a along the horizontal direction, making a and b together do uniformly accelerated linear motion along a smooth horizontal tabletop, the elongation of the spring is $x_2$, as shown in the figure. Try to compare the magnitude relationship between $x_1$ and $x_2$.
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
First describe the image: In the left figure, object a is above and object b is below; the two are connected by a vertical light spring, and the external force F acts vertically upward on a; in the right figure, object b, the spring, and object a are placed in sequence on a smooth horizontal tabletop, and the external force F acts horizontally to the right on a.
Then reason: Suppose the masses of the two objects are respectively m1 and m2. When pulling vertically upward, take a and b as a whole as the object of study, there is F-(m1+m2)g=(m1+m2)a1, so a1=F/(m1+m2)-g. Then analyze object b: in the vertical direction the spring tension T1 is upward, and the weight m2g is downward, therefore T1-m2g=m2a1; substituting a1 gives T1=m2F/(m1+m2). When pulling horizontally, take a and b as a whole as the object of study; on the smooth horizontal plane, in the horizontal direction there is only the external force F, so F=(m1+m2)a2, giving a2=F/(m1+m2). Then analyze object b: in the horizontal direction the spring tension T2 provides its acceleration, therefore T2=m2a2=m2F/(m1+m2). Thus T1=T2. A light spring satisfies Hooke's law T=kx, and the spring is the same, so x1=x2.
